questions.question: Your restoring force is written restoringForce = stiffness * displacement, with no minus sign. There is no damping. You release the mass from rest 1 m to the right of equilibrium. What happens?
answers: It swings back and forth around equilibrium.
It speeds away from equilibrium and never comes back.
It returns to equilibrium and stops there.

questions.question: A damped spring’s mass is to the right of equilibrium and moving left, back toward it. Which describes the damping force right now?
answers: Pushes left, stronger the farther the mass is from equilibrium.
Pushes left, stronger the faster the mass moves.
Pushes right, stronger the farther the mass is from equilibrium.
Pushes right, stronger the faster the mass moves.
Clamp deltaTime to at most 1/30 s.

questions.question: A crate’s spring computes stiffness and damping from mass, frequency, and damping ratio. It uses 2 Hz and damping ratio 0.5. You change the mass from 1 to 3 and repeat the same release. Which settings preserve its motion?

A menu panel starts from rest and springs toward a fixed equilibrium at 2 Hz with damping ratio 1. The spring is simulated accurately at all four settings. Which change makes it settle sooner without overshooting?
A button’s scale starts at rest at 1.0 and is controlled by a damped spring. When pressed, it should animate to 0.9, then settle there while held. Which change produces this behavior?
answers: Set the spring’s current value to 0.9.

questions.question: A 6 Hz spring with damping ratio 0.3 uses semi-implicit Euler and the raw frame time. It behaves at 60 fps but flies off at 15 fps. Which change fixes this while keeping the frequency setting at 6 Hz?
answers: Clamp deltaTime to at most 1/30 s.
Clamp deltaTime to at most 1/10 s.
